note: declared per sample. the platform is NOT inferable from the object.

original_st.name: Spatial Transcriptomics (Stahl 2016, KTH / Spatial Transcriptomics AB)
original_st.note: pitch corrected 2026-08-12 from 200um against the lattice. NOT Visium.
original_st.position_note: spots carries 6 columns: x,y (integer array grid), new_x,new_y (adjusted array), pixel_x,pixel_y (image pixels). every script reads the pixel pair - 34 occurrences, no other pair used. microns come from spot_pitch_um, never from these.
original_st.um_per_pixel_note: 150um pitch / 161.6px nearest-neighbour. the lattice has been measured twice: 161.6px is the nearest-neighbour figure in CLAUDE.md and docs/data_structure_flow.md; 158.6px is the median first-neighbour distance on CN1/C1 (design/progress.md F1), which gives 0.9458. this value uses the first, the he_tile micron figure uses the second. nothing in the package reads either, and a derived micron figure should name which one it used. this measurement supersedes 1.2195 as a description of the lattice. it does NOT replace 1.2195 as the scale the cached Novae embeddings were computed at - see st_graph.scale_to_microns.

st_graph.note: bare Delaunay, as the published grid was built. Delaunay creates long boundary edges on this lattice - max 4550px against a 215px mean - so a radius cap is a reasonable alternative, but it changes H1/H2 numbers. it therefore becomes a DECLARED alternative run as its own arm and evaluated, never a silent switch.
st_graph.scale_note: the value the cached Novae embeddings were computed with: 200 / 164, set as novae.settings.scale_to_microns in notebooks/embeddings/novae_st_embeddings.ipynb before compute_representations, and recorded as um_per_pixel_spot in the run manifest. it is an input, not an annotation: Novae 1.0.3 passes each edge length to the GAT as distance x scale_to_microns / 20 (novae/data/dataset.py; edge_dim=1 in novae/module/encode.py). the Delaunay topology is scale-invariant; the edge features are not. the 164px in that ratio was itself an estimate, so against the measured lattice the edge features are 1.29x (vs 0.9458) to 1.31x (vs 0.9282) what the 150um pitch implies. how much that moves the embeddings is unmeasured.

scale_declared_alternative.rule: spot_pitch_um / nearest-neighbour px, in the coordinate space passed to Novae
scale_declared_alternative.why_unset: the two recorded nearest-neighbour measurements give 0.9282 and 0.9458. the value is fixed when the arm is run, against a stated measurement.
scale_declared_alternative.question: does the lattice-true edge scale move the ST embeddings enough to change H1, H2 or H3?

image_pyramid.note: spot coordinates are recorded in HE-small space and scaled to the HD level before cropping. measured, not assumed: nearest-neighbour spacing is 158.6 px small / 528.7 px HD on CN1/C1.

he_tile.note: tiles are 95.9 um at extraction level. the code constant read 128 um and assumed a 200 um pitch (patch_px = 128 * nn_hd / pitch, so the pitch is an INPUT to the crop size, not a label); at the measured 150 um pitch that crop covers 95.9 um. corrected 2026-09-11. the published grid is unaffected as a COMPARISON - every arm saw the same tiles - but a 95.9 um square has half-width 48.0 um against a 50 um spot radius, so each spot was clipped by ~2 um PER SIDE (half-width 47.95 um against a 50 um radius) and the H&E arm under-sampled every spot.

declared_alternative.why: the first crop that fully contains a 100 um spot, with margin. run as its own arm and evaluated - it changes every H&E embedding and therefore H1, H2 and H3, so it is never a silent fix.
declared_alternative.question: does covering the whole spot change H1?

he_tile.identity_note: the run identity hashes tile_px_hd, the integer that sized the crop - never tile_um, which is derived from a measured nearest-neighbour distance and would move the identity if anyone re-measures it.

pitch_correction_consequences.novae: REAL, SIZE UNMEASURED. corrected 2026-09-15 from 'annotation only'. 1.2195 was set as novae.settings.scale_to_microns before the representations were computed, and Novae uses it to scale every edge feature the GAT reads. the neighbour graph is unaffected; the edge features are 1.29-1.31x too large against the 150um pitch. the cached embeddings are internally consistent and every arm read the same ones, so the ten-arm comparison stands as a comparison. whether a lattice-true scale changes any result is the declared alternative at st_graph.scale_declared_alternative.
pitch_correction_consequences.virchow2: REAL. the 200 um pitch sized the crop, so tiles are 95.9 um rather than the 128 um the constant named. cached embeddings are internally consistent and the ten-arm comparison stands; the tile is smaller than the spot it represents.
pitch_correction_consequences.why_here: the pitch correction reaches both encoders - the H&E crop size and the Novae edge features. a reader should find both in one place rather than discovering either from the code.

nearest_neighbour_px.note: two measurements of the same spacing in HE-small coordinates, 1.9% apart. recorded side by side so a derived micron figure can say which it used.

samples_note: keyed by CANONICAL sample id - {patient}_{slide}_{position} - which is what the inventory, the embedding cache and the niche join all use. re-keyed from {slide}_{position} on 2026-09-15: the old keys named the pre-ingest byArray layout, so every sample read as undeclared and the platform step failed on all 280. the patient prefix matters because a slide/position pair is not cohort-unique on its own in every cohort.

CN32_D2.why: declared in the source layout and absent from the canonical set - no HD image, so it cannot enter the morphology arm. see data/canonical/ingest.json#skipped
